objective_for_doctor: A 30-year-old Female patient presents to the clinic. Chief complaint: I have lower chest pain, sharp pain, and right breast pain.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Hi doctor. I’m having sharp pain in my lower chest and right breast pain. I also feel really short of breath, like I’m dying or I was about to die, and I’m sweating a lot. The pain started pretty fast and feels around 5 out of 10, mostly on the right side.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—first, when did the pain start and is it worse with deep breaths or lying down? Also, do you have any fever, cough, or recent long travel/surgery, and are you on birth control or pregnant?

The pain started pretty quickly, like within a short time—about a 6 out of 10 speed. I’m not sure if it’s worse with deep breaths or lying down; I haven’t really checked that. I don’t have fever or cough, and I haven’t had recent long travel or surgery. I’m not pregnant and I’m not on birth control.

Doctor: I need to check a few danger signs—right now, are you having palpitations or fainting, and do you have any leg swelling/pain on either side? If yes, this could be a blood clot, so we should act fast.  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: ECG; REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray; REQUEST TEST: D-dimer (or CT_Pulmonary_Angiography if high risk)

No, I’m not fainting and I don’t feel palpitations. I also don’t have leg swelling or leg pain on either side. If you need it, I’m okay with getting an ECG, a chest X-ray, and the blood test you mentioned.

Doctor: I’m glad you don’t have fainting, palpitations, or leg swelling. Next questions: is the pain reproducible when you press on the right chest/breast area, and do you notice any rash or recent injury/heavy lifting?  

Doctor: REQUEST TEST: ECG; REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray; REQUEST TEST: D-dimer

I think it might be a bit reproducible when I press on the right breast/chest area, but I’m not 100% sure. I don’t have any rash, and I don’t remember any recent injury or heavy lifting. If you need to, I’m okay to do the ECG, chest X-ray, and the D-dimer blood test.

Doctor: Thank you—given your sharp right-sided pain that may be touch-reproducible, and the lack of fever/cough or clot risk factors (no birth control, no travel/surgery, no leg swelling), I suspect a chest wall or breast-related cause (e.g., costochondritis/musculoskeletal pain) but I still need to rule out dangerous causes; REQUEST TEST: ECG; REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray; REQUEST TEST: D-dimer.  
Doctor: While we’re waiting, are you having any new cough, vomiting of blood, or one-sided leg symptoms, and do you have asthma or any recent viral illness?
No new cough, and I don’t have vomiting of blood. I don’t have one-sided leg symptoms. I do have asthma, and I haven’t had a recent viral illness that I know of.

Doctor: Given sharp right-sided lower chest/breast pain that may be reproducible with pressing, no cough/fever/hemoptysis, no clot risk factors, and asthma history, the most likely cause is musculoskeletal chest wall pain (costochondritis) though we must still rule out cardiac/PE with your ECG, chest X-ray, and D-dimer.  

Doctor: After the tests return, I’ll decide; do you have the test results yet, especially the ECG and D-dimer, and is your pain worse with twisting or taking a deep breath?

I don’t have the test results yet—ECG and the D-dimer haven’t come back for me. And I haven’t noticed for sure if it’s worse with twisting or with a deep breath; I can tell you it feels sharp and right-sided, and it gets worse when I’m thinking about it and I get really scared/sweaty.

Doctor: I’m still concerned we must rule out heart/lung causes while your tests are pending—please answer quickly: does the pain get worse with a deep breath, and can you point with one finger to the exact spot that reproduces the pain when you press?  
Doctor: Also, did the sweating and “about to die” feeling start at the same time as the pain, or did it come after?

Yes, it feels worse when I take a deep breath, and I can point to one exact spot on the right lower chest/breast area where pressing reproduces the pain. The sweating and the “about to die” feeling started basically at the same time as the pain.

Doctor: With pleuritic-type pain (worse on deep breath) plus an exact focal tender spot that reproduces with pressing, and no clot risk factors or leg symptoms, this most fits **costochondritis/chest wall pain**, though we still must ensure your **ECG, chest X-ray, and D-dimer** are negative for cardiac/PE causes.  
Doctor: Do you have any test results back for the **ECG, chest X-ray, and D-dimer** yet?
No—so far I haven’t seen any results back yet for the ECG, chest X-ray, or the D-dimer.

Doctor: While your ECG, chest X-ray, and D-dimer are still pending, I want to make sure there’s no hidden emergency: are you currently oxygen-limited or struggling to speak full sentences, and do you have a new wheeze/major asthma flare right now? Also—on a 0–10 scale, is the pain now the same as when it started, or getting rapidly worse?  
Doctor: If those are stable, with focal one-finger reproducible right chest/breast pain plus pleuritic worsening and no clot/fever/cough/hemoptysis risk factors, the leading diagnosis is **costochondritis/chest wall pain**, and I’ll proceed assuming serious causes are unlikely unless your tests come back abnormal.  
DIAGNOSIS READY: Costochondritis (musculoskeletal chest wall pain)
